title: ITR Filed & Verified? How the Income Tax Department Spots Mismatches
description: The Income Tax Department (ITD) uses technology to cross-verify information declared in your ITR with data from various sources like Form 26AS, Annual Informa.

faq.q: What is the difference between AIS and Form 26AS?
faq.a: AIS (Annual Information Statement) is a comprehensive statement covering all financial transactions reported to the ITD, including interest, dividends, securities transactions, and more. Form 26AS primarily focuses on TDS/TCS and certain high-value transactions. AIS is broader in scope.

faq.q: How long does the Income Tax Department have to send a notice?
faq.a: The time limits for sending notices vary by section. For instance, a defective return notice (Section 139(9)) is typically issued shortly after filing. A scrutiny notice (Section 143(2)) can be issued within six months from the end of the financial year in which the return was filed. Notices for income escaping assessment (Section 148) have longer periods, up to 3 or 10 years depending on the amount.

faq.q: What happens if I ignore an ITD notice?
faq.a: Ignoring an ITD notice can lead to serious consequences, including penalties, higher tax demands, initiation of assessment proceedings ex-parte (without your input), and even prosecution in severe cases. Always respond promptly and accurately.

faq.q: Can I revise my ITR after receiving a notice?
faq.a: Yes, in many cases, especially for notices under Section 139(9) (defective return) or intimation under Section 143(1) that highlight a mismatch, you can file a revised return to correct the errors. However, for scrutiny notices (Section 143(2)) or income escaping assessment notices (Section 148), you need to respond to the specific queries raised.

faq.q: What if the information in my AIS is incorrect?
faq.a: If you find incorrect information in your AIS, you can submit feedback on the e-filing portal. The ITD will then forward this feedback to the reporting entity (e.g., bank, employer) for verification and correction. It's crucial to ensure your AIS is accurate.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to report exempt income in my ITR?
faq.a: Yes, while exempt income is not taxable, it is generally mandatory to report it in your ITR, especially if it exceeds certain thresholds. This helps the ITD get a complete picture of your financial standing and avoids potential mismatches.

faq.q: What is the deadline to respond to an ITD notice?
faq.a: The deadline to respond is specified in the notice itself, typically ranging from 15 to 30 days. It is crucial to adhere to these deadlines. If you need more time, you can often request an extension from the Assessing Officer, stating valid reasons.
